content.content:
1	# Feature Specification: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch was created automatically; none of this repo's extension hooks are configured)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-10-19
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG): Build the conversation with the AI agent, which answers with context from the user's previous entries, per docs/input/requirements.md section 1 (RF04) and its acceptance criteria. Prototype states: 'Tela 1 — Home/Chat' (default), 'Streaming', 'Falha ao gerar resposta', 'Offline'; 'Tela 3 — Menu lateral' with the session list and the new-conversation action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4). Backend: POST /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions, GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages, POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages (SSE), POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry (requirements, section 6.3). Depends on F000, RF03. Do not implement features of later units, extension features (requirements section 2), or change the backend."
10	
11	## Clarifications
12	
13	### Session 2026-10-19
14	
15	- Q: `POST /chat/sessions` accepts an optional `title`, the backend has no auto-titling logic of its own, and no endpoint exists to rename a session afterward — so whatever the app does at creation time is permanent for that conversation. Should the app send a title derived from the first message, or never send one? → A: The app derives a short title client-side from the first message's text (trimmed, capped to a short preview length) and sends it in `POST /chat/sessions`'s `title` field at the moment that first message creates the session. This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
16	- Q: `GET /chat/sessions` is cursor-paginated (`cursor`/`limit`, default 20, max 50) and its items carry no documented sort order; the prototype's side-menu extract shows a flat "CONVERSAS" list with no load-more control. How should the side menu order and page through sessions once an account has more than one page's worth? → A: The list is ordered by most recent activity (`lastUserMessageAt`, descending; a session always has a `lastUserMessageAt` by the time it is listed, since sessions are only created together with their first message), and the side menu fetches further pages via `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the "CONVERSAS" section (the same infinite-scroll pattern already established for RF07's own list) — so no conversation ever becomes unreachable as the account accumulates sessions beyond a single page. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
17	- Q: `docs/input/requirements.md` §6.3 marks both `GET /chat/sessions` and `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` as "works offline (cache)," without scoping that to only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped. Does offline mode cover every previously-opened conversation, or only the one open at disconnect? → A: The cache (and offline readability) covers every chat session the user has opened at least once while online — both the side menu's own session list and the message history of each previously-opened conversation remain browsable and switchable while offline; only creating a session, sending a message, and retrying require connectivity (already covered by FR-012). Selecting a conversation from the side menu that was never loaded while online, while currently offline, shows the standard no-connection state (no cached data to fall back to) rather than any content. (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)
18	
19	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
20	
21	### User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1)
22	
23	A user opens the chat and asks the AI agent something related to their life, without repeating what they already wrote elsewhere. The agent's answer reflects relevant things the user recorded before, not just the current message in isolation, and the exchange stays on screen as a normal, persisted conversation the user can come back to.
24	
25	**Why this priority**: This is the entire premise of RF04 — "memory" via semantic search over past entries. Without it, the screen is just a generic chat window with no connection to the rest of the product.
26	
27	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by seeding an account with a prior entry about a specific topic, sending a chat message that references that topic without quoting it verbatim, and confirming the agent's response demonstrates awareness of the seeded entry's content.
28	
29	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
30	
31	1. **Given** the user has at least one prior entry about a specific topic, **When** they send a chat message related to that topic, **Then** the agent's response reflects information from that entry, even though the message itself never restated it.
32	2. **Given** a conversation already has one or more exchanges, **When** the user leaves the screen and returns later (including after an app restart), **Then** the full exchange history is still present, in the same order, without needing to be resent.
33	3. **Given** the user sends a chat message, **When** the message is accepted, **Then** it is stored and displayed as part of the conversation but does **not** create a journal entry — chat messages are conversational only, with no automatic persistence as an entry (the one exception, an explicit save action, belongs to a later unit and is out of scope here).
34	
35	---
36	
37	### User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)
38	
39	While waiting for or reading a response, the user can always tell, at a glance, which of three things is happening: the answer is still arriving, it finished successfully, or it failed — and a response that stops arriving partway through never just vanishes.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: RF04's acceptance criteria explicitly require these three states and the no-disappearing-partial-message rule; without a clear, honest status, users cannot trust the chat enough to rely on it.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by sending a message and observing the UI progress through the "processing/streaming" state into either "complete response" or "error," and separately by forcing a connection drop mid-response and confirming the partial text stays visible with a failure indication instead of disappearing.
44	
45	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
46	
47	1. **Given** the user has just sent a message, **When** the agent begins producing a reply, **Then** the response is revealed progressively (streaming) with a visible in-progress indicator, distinct from a finished message.
48	2. **Given** a response finishes streaming normally, **When** the last token arrives, **Then** the message is shown in its final, complete form with its timestamp, no longer carrying any in-progress indicator.
49	3. **Given** the connection drops, or the backend returns an error, while a response is still arriving, **When** that happens, **Then** whatever text had already arrived stays visible, together with a clear failure indication in place of the timestamp — the message is never removed or left in an ambiguous unfinished-looking state.
50	
51	---
52	
53	### User Story 3 - Recovering from a failed response without losing the conversation (Priority: P2)
54	
55	A response fails or is cut short. The user taps the failed message and gets a fresh attempt at an answer to the same question, without having to retype it, without creating a duplicate question in the history, and without disturbing the rest of the conversation.
56	
57	**Why this priority**: A direct extension of Story 2's failure state — the failure indication is only useful if there's a documented way out of it, and the requirement calls this out explicitly ("a way to try again" is part of RF04's own scope).
58	
59	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by forcing a response failure, tapping the failed message to retry, and confirming a new response is generated for the same original question, with the user's question appearing exactly once in the history.
60	
61	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
62	
63	1. **Given** a message shows the "Falha ao gerar resposta" state, **When** the user taps it, **Then** a new response attempt starts for that same original question, going through the same processing/streaming → complete/error states as a normal response.
64	2. **Given** a retry is in progress or has completed, **When** the history is inspected, **Then** the user's original question appears exactly once — retrying never duplicates the question, only replaces the failed answer with a new attempt.
65	3. **Given** the retry itself fails again, **When** that happens, **Then** the message returns to the same failure state with the same way to try again — retrying is not limited to a single attempt.
66	
67	---
68	
69	### User Story 4 - Organizing conversations from the side menu (Priority: P2)
70	
71	A user wants to start a brand-new conversation without losing an existing one, and wants to see and return to past conversations by name and recency from the side menu.
72	
73	**Why this priority**: RF04's own scope explicitly includes the side menu's session list and "Novo Chat" action (prototype extract, sections 2.2 and 4) — without it, a user has no way to manage more than one conversation at a time.
74	
75	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by having at least one existing conversation, opening the side menu, confirming it lists past sessions with a title and timestamp, tapping "Novo Chat," confirming the chat screen shows an empty conversation, and confirming the prior conversation is unchanged when reopened from the list.
76	
77	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
78	
79	1. **Given** the user has one or more existing conversations, **When** they open the side menu, **Then** a "CONVERSAS" section lists each one with a title and a timestamp.
80	2. **Given** the side menu is open, **When** the user taps the new-conversation action ("Novo Chat"), **Then** the chat screen shows an empty conversation, ready to accept a first message, without discarding any previous conversation.
81	3. **Given** the user selects a past conversation from the list, **When** it opens, **Then** its full message history is shown exactly as it was left.
82	
83	---
84	
85	### User Story 5 - Reading history while offline (Priority: P3)
86	
87	A user without a connection can still read everything they already loaded, but cannot send anything new, and is told clearly why.
88	
89	**Why this priority**: Explicitly one of the four required prototype states for this screen, and it protects against the worse failure mode of a chat screen that looks broken or loses content when connectivity drops — but it is a secondary concern relative to the core conversation and failure-recovery loops above.
90	
91	**Independent Test**: Can be fully tested by loading a conversation, simulating a loss of connectivity, confirming the existing history stays visible and scrollable, confirming the send control is disabled with an explanatory banner, and confirming sending is not possible until connectivity returns.
92	
93	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
94	
95	1. **Given** a conversation is already loaded, **When** the device goes offline, **Then** the existing message history remains visible and scrollable, and a banner explains that new messages are blocked.
96	2. **Given** the device is offline, **When** the user looks at the composer, **Then** the send control is visibly disabled — no message can be sent until the connection returns.
97	3. **Given** the connection returns, **When** the user resumes using the screen, **Then** the send control re-enables and new messages can be sent normally.
98	4. **Given** the user has previously opened more than one conversation while online, **When** the device goes offline and the user switches between those previously-opened conversations from the side menu, **Then** each one's cached history is shown exactly as it was left, not just the conversation open at the moment connectivity dropped.
99	
100	---
101	
102	### Edge Cases
103	
104	- The user tries to send an empty or whitespace-only message: the send control stays disabled/inactive, and no request is made.
105	- A message at or near the backend's maximum length is sent: the system either prevents exceeding that maximum before sending or surfaces the backend's resulting validation error clearly, without losing the text the user typed.
106	- A message is sent while a previous response in the same conversation is still streaming, or is sitting in the failed/"tap to retry" state: the composer stays disabled until that turn resolves (completes or is retried to a new resolution), so a session never has two responses racing at once.
107	- The session expires (RF03/RF07's existing "Sessão expirada" behavior) while a response is mid-stream or while viewing history: the existing overlay is shown, history and scroll position are preserved underneath it, and once the user re-authenticates, the conversation resumes exactly where it was — this unit reuses that behavior rather than redefining it.
108	- The user navigates away from a conversation (e.g., via the side menu) while a response is still streaming: when the user returns to that conversation, the message reflects whatever the backend ultimately recorded for it (complete or failed) rather than being stuck in a stale in-progress state tied to a connection that no longer exists.
109	- An account has zero conversations yet (first-ever use of chat): the chat screen still shows a ready-to-use empty conversation, and a session is created at the point the first message is actually sent.
110	- The user retries a failed message that is not the most recent message in the conversation: the retry still succeeds and only affects that specific message's response, leaving every later message in the conversation untouched.
111	- An account has more conversations than fit in one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` (more than its default/max `limit`): scrolling to the bottom of the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section fetches the next page via `cursor` rather than silently stopping at the first page.
112	- The user is offline and selects, from the side menu, a conversation that was never opened while online: no cached data exists for it, so the screen shows the standard no-connection state instead of any content, distinct from the normal offline case of browsing an already-cached conversation.
113	- Opening the side menu's conversation list, the export job, dashboard, filters, action-plan board, and every other screen or action not named in this feature's scope: unaffected by this unit and not touched by it.
114	
115	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
116	
117	### Functional Requirements
118	
119	- **FR-001**: The system MUST let an authenticated user send a text message in an active conversation (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`) and receive a response generated with the help of the user's own previously captured entries — the response MUST be able to reflect information from a prior entry that the user's message does not itself restate.
120	- **FR-002**: Every message the user sends and every response the agent produces MUST be persisted as part of the conversation (`chat_messages`) and MUST still be present, in the same order, the next time that conversation is opened — including after the app is closed and reopened (`GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages`).
121	- **FR-003**: Sending a chat message MUST NOT create a journal entry under any circumstance handled by this unit; the only path from a chat message to a persisted entry is the explicit save action of a later unit (RF10), which this unit does not implement.
122	- **FR-004**: While a response is being generated, the system MUST render it in a visibly distinct "processing/streaming" state (content revealed progressively, in-progress indicator) and MUST transition it to one of exactly two end states: "complete response" (final text, timestamp shown, no in-progress indicator) or an error state ("Falha ao gerar resposta," shown in place of the timestamp). 123	- **FR-005**: If the response stream is interrupted before completion (connection drop, backend error, or any other cause), the system MUST keep whatever partial text had already arrived visible, together with the failure indication — it MUST NOT remove, hide, or blank out a partial message.
124	- **FR-006**: A message in the error state MUST be tappable to trigger a retry (`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry`) that regenerates the response to that same original question. 125	- **FR-007**: While a response in the current conversation is streaming or sitting in the error state awaiting retry, the system MUST keep the message-send control disabled, re-enabling it only once that response reaches a final state (complete, or retried to a new resolution) — so a single conversation never has two responses in flight at once.
126	- **FR-008**: The side menu MUST show a "CONVERSAS" section listing the user's existing conversations (`GET /chat/sessions`), each with its title and a timestamp, ordered by most recent activity (latest `lastUserMessageAt` first). 127	- **FR-009**: The side menu MUST offer a "Novo Chat" action that opens the chat screen in an empty conversation state, ready to accept a first message, without discarding or altering any existing conversation. Selecting an existing conversation from the list MUST open it with its full message history intact, exactly as it was left.
128	- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it. 129	- **FR-011**: While the device is offline, the system MUST keep every previously-opened conversation's history, and the side menu's own "CONVERSAS" list, visible, scrollable, and switchable from the local cache — not only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped — MUST disable the send control, and MUST show an explanatory message that new messages are blocked until the connection returns. Selecting a conversation that was never opened while online, while currently offline, MUST show the standard no-connection state rather than any content, since nothing was ever cached for it. Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.
130	- **FR-012**: The system MUST NOT attempt to create a new conversation or send/retry a message while offline — both actions require a connection and MUST be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed.
131	- **FR-013**: The screen MUST reuse the existing session-expiration handling (RF03/RF07's "Sessão expirada" overlay: history and scroll position preserved, re-authentication returning to the same conversation state) rather than introducing a separate expiration treatment for chat.
132	- **FR-014**: This unit MUST NOT implement the "save message as entry" button (RF10), the proactive-insight card (RF08), AI-persona selection as an active setting (extension, requirements section 2 — persona is only read at session creation as whatever the backend already returns), or any change to the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.
133	
134	### Key Entities
135	
136	- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
137	- **Chat Message**: One turn inside a Chat Session — either the user's question or the agent's response — with its content, its position in the conversation, and its status (still arriving, complete, or failed). A failed message is the one eligible for retry; retrying produces a new resolution for the same original question rather than a new message pair.
138	- **Context used for a response**: The set of the user's own prior entries the agent draws on to ground a given response. It is retrieved automatically for every response and is not displayed to the user as a separate citation list — the prototype defines no such element — but it is what makes a response "grounded" rather than generic, per User Story 1.
139	
140	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
141	
142	### Measurable Outcomes
143	
144	- **SC-001**: When a seeded prior entry exists on a topic, a chat message about that topic that does not restate the entry's content still produces a response reflecting that entry's information, in 100% of tested cases.
145	- **SC-002**: Every sent or retried message ends in exactly one of the three defined states (streaming → complete, or streaming → error) with zero cases observed stuck in an undefined or ambiguous state.
146	- **SC-003**: In 100% of forced stream-interruption scenarios, the partial response text remains visible on screen together with its failure indication — never disappearing.
147	- **SC-004**: Across repeated retries of the same failed message, the user's original question appears exactly once in the conversation history, with zero observed duplicates.
148	- **SC-005**: Conversation history is preserved exactly (same messages, same order) across an app restart and across switching away from and back to a conversation via the side menu, in 100% of tested cases.
149	- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.
150	- **SC-007**: On an account with more conversations than one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` returns, 100% of them remain reachable from the side menu by scrolling, with zero conversations permanently hidden.
151	
152	## Assumptions
153	
154	- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in (if any exist); when none exist yet, the screen shows the same empty, ready-to-send state "Novo Chat" also produces.
155	- The "context" step of the backend's streaming sequence (`message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`) is an internal signal the client may use to drive its own progress indicator, not a citation list rendered to the user — the prototype defines no UI for displaying which entries were used.
156	- A session's `personaSnapshot` (requirements section 2's persona extension) is read and stored as whatever the backend returns at session creation; this unit does not add any UI for choosing or changing it.
157	- Network-error handling for this screen's write calls (send, retry, create session) follows the same retryable/non-retryable pattern already established project-wide (RNF09) — no new error-presentation style is introduced specifically for chat.
158	- Every chat session is created with a client-derived title (see FR-010), so the generic placeholder in the side-menu list is a defensive fallback for an unexpected empty title rather than the normal case; the exact wording of both the derived-title preview length and the fallback placeholder is a presentation detail left to implementation.
159	- The composer's existing disabled-by-default rendering (already scaffolded by F000) becomes conditionally enabled by this unit whenever there is non-empty text to send and no response currently in flight or awaiting retry for that conversation — it does not require a separate redesign of the composer itself.

**Created**: 2026-10-19

**Status**: Draft

## Clarifications

This is the only mechanism that can ever give a conversation a human-recognizable name, and User Story 4 explicitly requires the side menu to let users find past conversations "by name." (Resolved by technical judgment per user direction, applying Constitution Principle I.)

Retrying MUST remain available after a retry itself fails, with no fixed limit on the number of attempts, and MUST remain available on any message in the error state regardless of how much later conversation exists after it.
- **FR-007**: While a response in the current conversation is streaming or sitting in the error state awaiting retry, the system MUST keep the message-send control disabled, re-enabling it only once that response reaches a final state (complete, or retried to a new resolution) — so a single conversation never has two responses in flight at once.
- **FR-008**: The side menu MUST show a "CONVERSAS" section listing the user's existing conversations (`GET /chat/sessions`), each with its title and a timestamp, ordered by most recent activity (latest `lastUserMessageAt` first). If the account has more sessions than fit in one backend page, the list MUST fetch further pages via the endpoint's `cursor` as the user scrolls to the bottom of the section, so every conversation stays reachable.
- **FR-009**: The side menu MUST offer a "Novo Chat" action that opens the chat screen in an empty conversation state, ready to accept a first message, without discarding or altering any existing conversation. Selecting an existing conversation from the list MUST open it with its full message history intact, exactly as it was left.
- **FR-010**: A new conversation (`POST /chat/sessions`) MUST only be created at the point a first message is actually sent into an empty conversation state — opening an empty conversation state (via "Novo Chat," or on an account with no conversations yet) MUST NOT by itself create a session with no messages in it. That creation call MUST include a `title` derived from the first message's own text (a short, trimmed preview), so the new conversation has a distinguishable, human-recognizable name in the side menu from the moment it exists — the backend has no auto-titling of its own and no later rename endpoint.
- **FR-011**: While the device is offline, the system MUST keep every previously-opened conversation's history, and the side menu's own "CONVERSAS" list, visible, scrollable, and switchable from the local cache — not only the one conversation that happened to be open when connectivity dropped — MUST disable the send control, and MUST show an explanatory message that new messages are blocked until the connection returns. Selecting a conversation that was never opened while online, while currently offline, MUST show the standard no-connection state rather than any content, since nothing was ever cached for it. Sending MUST become possible again as soon as connectivity is restored, with no manual reset required.
- **FR-012**: The system MUST NOT attempt to create a new conversation or send/retry a message while offline — both actions require a connection and MUST be blocked client-side rather than attempted and failed.
- **FR-013**: The screen MUST reuse the existing session-expiration handling (RF03/RF07's "Sessão expirada" overlay: history and scroll position preserved, re-authentication returning to the same conversation state) rather than introducing a separate expiration treatment for chat.
- **FR-014**: This unit MUST NOT implement the "save message as entry" button (RF10), the proactive-insight card (RF08), AI-persona selection as an active setting (extension, requirements section 2 — persona is only read at session creation as whatever the backend already returns), or any change to the backend, its API contract, or its configuration.

### Key Entities

- **Chat Session**: One conversation thread, identified by an id, with a title derived client-side from its first message at creation time and shown in the side menu's "CONVERSAS" section (a defensive generic placeholder is shown only if a session is ever encountered with an empty title), the persona that was in effect when it was created (read-only here — not user-editable in this unit), and timestamps including when it was created and when it last received a user message (the latter drives the side menu's ordering).
- **Chat Message**: One turn inside a Chat Session — either the user's question or the agent's response — with its content, its position in the conversation, and its status (still arriving, complete, or failed). A failed message is the one eligible for retry; retrying produces a new resolution for the same original question rather than a new message pair.
- **Context used for a response**: The set of the user's own prior entries the agent draws on to ground a given response. It is retrieved automatically for every response and is not displayed to the user as a separate citation list — the prototype defines no such element — but it is what makes a response "grounded" rather than generic, per User Story 1.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: When a seeded prior entry exists on a topic, a chat message about that topic that does not restate the entry's content still produces a response reflecting that entry's information, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-002**: Every sent or retried message ends in exactly one of the three defined states (streaming → complete, or streaming → error) with zero cases observed stuck in an undefined or ambiguous state.
- **SC-003**: In 100% of forced stream-interruption scenarios, the partial response text remains visible on screen together with its failure indication — never disappearing.
- **SC-004**: Across repeated retries of the same failed message, the user's original question appears exactly once in the conversation history, with zero observed duplicates.
- **SC-005**: Conversation history is preserved exactly (same messages, same order) across an app restart and across switching away from and back to a conversation via the side menu, in 100% of tested cases.
- **SC-006**: While offline, 100% of the history of every previously-opened conversation stays readable and switchable from the side menu (not only the one open at disconnect), and the send control is visibly disabled for the entire duration of the outage, re-enabling within one interaction of connectivity returning.
- **SC-007**: On an account with more conversations than one backend page of `GET /chat/sessions` returns, 100% of them remain reachable from the side menu by scrolling, with zero conversations permanently hidden.

## Assumptions

- A conversation ("session") is created lazily, only when the user actually sends a first message into an empty conversation state, rather than eagerly when "Novo Chat" is tapped or when the chat screen is simply opened — this keeps the backend free of empty sessions and matches `POST /chat/sessions` accepting no required `title`. Re-opening the app resumes whichever conversation the user was last in (if any exist); when none exist yet, the screen shows the same empty, ready-to-send state "Novo Chat" also produces.
- The "context" step of the backend's streaming sequence (`message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`) is an internal signal the client may use to drive its own progress indicator, not a citation list rendered to the user — the prototype defines no UI for displaying which entries were used.
- A session's `personaSnapshot` (requirements section 2's persona extension) is read and stored as whatever the backend returns at session creation; this unit does not add any UI for choosing or changing it.
- Network-error handling for this screen's write calls (send, retry, create session) follows the same retryable/non-retryable pattern already established project-wide (RNF09) — no new error-presentation style is introduced specifically for chat.
- Every chat session is created with a client-derived title (see FR-010), so the generic placeholder in the side-menu list is a defensive fallback for an unexpected empty title rather than the normal case; the exact wording of both the derived-title preview length and the fallback placeholder is a presentation detail left to implementation.
- The composer's existing disabled-by-default rendering (already scaffolded by F000) becomes conditionally enabled by this unit whenever there is non-empty text to send and no response currently in flight or awaiting retry for that conversation — it does not require a separate redesign of the composer itself.

# Implementation Plan: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Branch**: `007-chat-memory-rag` (spec directory only — no git branch exists; none of this repo's extension
hooks are configured, per spec.md's own header)

**Date**: 2026-10-19 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/spec.md`, `docs/input/requirements.md` §1
(RF04), §6.3 (`chat-sessions-create`/`chat-sessions-list`/`chat-messages-list`/`chat-messages-send`/
`chat-messages-retry`), §8 (data model reference), §9 (stack), §10 (no new fixed parameter for this unit),
§13; `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`'s `/chat/sessions*` schemas; `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`;
`docs/input/backend/README.md`'s function-name mapping; `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md` §§2.2
("Tela 1 — Home/Chat", "Tela 3 — Menu lateral"), 3, 4, 6; and `.specify/memory/constitution.md`. Depends on
F000 (`specs/001-foundation/`) and RF03 (`specs/002-biometric-auth-vault/`), both already implemented — this
is the unit that makes Home/Chat's currently-inert, fully-disabled composer (F000's own scaffold,
`home_chat_shell_page.dart`) and the side menu's currently-static `AppDrawer` actually work.

## Summary

Home/Chat gains a live, persisted conversation with the backend's RAG-grounded agent
(`POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages`, SSE: `message_created -> context -> token* -> done|error`), and the side
menu's `AppDrawer` gains a paginated, offline-cached "CONVERSAS" list (`GET /chat/sessions`) plus a working
"Novo Chat" action. A new feature folder, `lib/features/chat/`, is added with its own three-layer structure:
`ChatSession`/`ChatMessage`/`ChatSessionsPage`/`ChatStreamEvent`/`ChatTitleDeriver` (domain), `ChatRemoteDataSource`/
`ChatLocalCache`/`ChatRepositoryImpl` (data), and two blocs — `ChatBloc` (the one live conversation: streaming,
retry, lazy session creation, composer gating) and `ChatSessionsBloc` (the side menu's own paginated list,
mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s RF07-established shape almost exactly, research.md R7). `core/network/ApiClient`
gains one new, chat-agnostic method, `sseStream()`, built on `dio`'s own `ResponseType.stream` with a
hand-rolled SSE frame parser (research.md R1) — no new package. `core/network/ConnectivityChecker` gains a
live `onConnectivityChanged` stream (research.md R8), layered on top of (not replacing) the existing
synchronous `hasConnection()` pre-check every write path in this app already uses. A new, Keychain-backed
`ChatLocalCache` (mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own pattern) persists the session list, each individually-
opened session's message history, and the last-active session id, satisfying spec.md's Clarification 3
(offline browsing covers every previously-opened conversation, not just the one open at disconnect) and its
own Assumptions (resuming the last conversation on app restart). A new chat message or its own session is
never created eagerly — only lazily, at the moment a first message is actually sent (FR-010) — and the title
sent with that creation call is derived client-side from the message's own text by a new, pure
`ChatTitleDeriver` (research.md R6), since the backend has no auto-titling or rename endpoint of its own. No
new `go_router` route is added: Home/Chat stays the one existing, unparameterized `/home` screen, swapping its
displayed conversation in place via the two blocs it's now provided with (research.md R7) — "Novo Chat" and
selecting a past conversation from the drawer are both in-place state transitions, not navigations.

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: Dart 3.13.4 / Flutter 3.47.5 (stable), pinned via `.fvmrc` — unchanged from
F000/RF01/RF02/RF03/RF06/RF07.

**Primary Dependencies**: No additions. Reuses the full existing stack — `flutter_bloc`, `fpdart`, `get_it`,
`equatable`, `dio` (via `ApiClient`, extended with `sseStream()`), `go_router` (no new route), `flutter_secure_storage`
(for the new `ChatLocalCache`), `connectivity_plus` (its own `onConnectivityChanged` stream, previously
unused — `ConnectivityChecker` only ever called `checkConnectivity()` once per check before this unit); dev-only
`mocktail`, `bloc_test`. SSE is consumed via a ~30-line hand-rolled parser over `dio`'s existing byte-stream
support, explicitly chosen over any third-party SSE package (research.md R1) — the OpenAPI contract's own
schema for both SSE operations is `content: text/event-stream` / `{type: string}`, i.e. genuinely no typed
shape to generate a client from.

**Storage**: One new on-device store, `ChatLocalCache` (research.md R4) — three independent
`flutter_secure_storage` keys (`chatSessionsLocalCache`, `chatMessagesLocalCache`, `chatLastActiveSessionId`),
same Keychain-backed, JSON-encoded mechanism `EntriesLocalCache` (RF01) already established for personal
content. No local database, no new third-party persistence package.

**Testing**: `flutter_test` + `bloc_test` + `mocktail`, unchanged tooling. Coverage via
`fvm flutter test --coverage`, same `lib/**/domain/**` lcov filter (RNF07), now additionally exercising
`chat_title_deriver.dart` (pure), `ChatMessage`'s status-transition shape, `ChatRepositoryImpl`'s
silent-refresh-and-retry branches (both the non-streaming shape reused verbatim from `EntriesRepositoryImpl`,
and the new first-frame-only streaming variant, research.md R3), and `ApiClient.sseStream()`'s own frame
parser (a `core/` addition — `test/core/network/`, mirroring where `error_mapper_test.dart`/similar already
live). `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` and `domain_purity_test.dart` both run unmodified against the new
`lib/features/chat/` folder with no exceptions needed.

**Target Platform**: iOS, portrait only — unchanged. No native project file touched.

**Project Type**: Same single Flutter mobile app. One new feature folder, `lib/features/chat/`
(domain/data/presentation, Principle V), plus two cross-cutting `core/network/` additions
(`ApiClient.sseStream()`/`SseFrame`, `ConnectivityChecker.onConnectivityChanged`) and in-place extensions to
`lib/features/home/` (`home_chat_shell_page.dart`'s composer, `app_drawer.dart`'s "CONVERSAS" section) and
`lib/core/routing/app_router.dart` (`/home`'s builder now wraps `MultiBlocProvider`). No backend/server code,
no change to `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`. No touch to `entries/`/`records/` — this unit never calls
`POST /entries` (FR-003/FR-014; that wiring belongs to RF10, explicitly out of scope).

**Performance Goals**: RNF01 unchanged. The optimistic local user+assistant placeholder pair (research.md R5)
is what keeps "a local action is reflected in the UI in under 100 ms" true for message-send despite the
network round-trip and SSE latency that necessarily follow it.

**Constraints**:
- No RF08 (proactive insight card)/RF10 (save-as-entry button)/persona-as-an-active-setting (extension) —
  `personaSnapshot` is read and stored exactly as the backend returns it at session creation, with no UI to
  change it (FR-014).
- No backend/contract/config change (FR-014) — `sseStream()`'s request shape and every parsed field name
  (research.md R2) are this app's own typed wrapper around what `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` and its
  own documented SSE sequence already describe; nothing new is sent the contract doesn't already define, and
  where the contract is silent on exact SSE field names, research.md documents the inferred shape explicitly
  as a judgment call rather than a verified fact.
- Clean Architecture, 3 layers per feature (Principle V) — `chat/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart`;
  no `package:flutter`, no `chat/data/` class (confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart`, unmodified).
  `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` depend only on `ChatRepository` (+ `ConnectivityChecker` for `ChatBloc` alone)
  — neither imports the other, nor `SessionBloc` (research.md R7; `no_bloc_imports_bloc_test.dart` unmodified,
  reinforced manually since both blocs sit in the same feature and so aren't mechanically checked against each
  other by that cross-feature-only test).
- "A single conversation never has two responses in flight at once" (FR-007) — the composer disables itself
  while `ChatReady.awaitingResponse` is true; no concurrent-request/generation-counter machinery is needed
  because no second write can even be dispatched while it's disabled (research.md R9).
- Zero visual values hardcoded outside `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` (Principle IV/RNF08) — every new widget
  (chat bubbles, offline banner, composer) reuses existing tokens only (data-model.md's mapping table); zero
  new color/spacing/radius tokens needed, since the prototype's own chat-screen palette (`colorChatBubbleUser`,
  `colorInfoOffline`, `colorError`, etc.) was already added to `design_tokens.dart` during F000.

**Scale/Scope**: 1 new feature folder (`chat/`) with 5 domain entities/helpers, 1 repository interface, 2 data
classes + 1 repository impl, 2 blocs (+events/states), 5 new presentation widgets; 2 extended `core/network/`
classes (`ApiClient`, `ConnectivityChecker`); 2 existing `home/` files extended in place
(`home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`); 1 route builder changed (`app_router.dart`'s `/home`); 5 new
DI registrations.

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-checked after Phase 1 design — see bottom of this section.*

| Principle / Standard | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| I. Product Source of Truth | PASS | `docs/input/` read-only. Every spot this plan resolves by reasonable technical judgment rather than reopening one of spec.md's own three already-resolved Clarifications — the SSE transport mechanism and inferred payload shapes (research.md R1/R2), mid-stream auth-expiry handling (R3), the local-cache shape (R4), optimistic local ids (R5), the title-preview length (R6), the two-bloc split and routing (R7), live-vs-synchronous offline handling (R8), single-flight gating (R9), retry's position-matching (R10), the GET-sourced `streaming`-status edge case (R11), the client-side length cap (R12), and why no extra use-case layer is introduced (R13) — is each built directly on spec.md's own FRs/Assumptions/Key Entities wording, never reopening a resolved Clarification. |

Backend Boundary | PASS | Only already-contracted functions called (`chat-sessions-create`, `chat-sessions-list`, `chat-messages-list`, `chat-messages-send`, `chat-messages-retry` — `docs/input/backend/README.md`'s own path→function table); no AI provider called directly by the app (the backend's own Claude Sonnet 5/Voyage AI calls stay entirely server-side, consumed here only as the SSE response). |

| V. Clean Architecture Folder Convention | PASS | `chat/domain/` imports only `equatable`/`fpdart` — confirmed against `domain_purity_test.dart` (unmodified, no exception needed). `ChatBloc`/`ChatSessionsBloc` each depend on exactly the repository (+ `ConnectivityChecker` for the former) they need, no cross-bloc import. |

### Source Code (repository root)

```text
cerne-ciclo-a/
└── lib/
    ├── core/
    │   ├── network/
    │   │   ├── api_client.dart                          # + sseStream() (research.md R1)
```

| Addition | Why Needed | Simpler Alternative Rejected Because |
|---|---|---|

direct, justified extension of an already-proven pattern (two blocs mirroring `RecordsBloc`'s own split; a
cache mirroring `EntriesLocalCache`'s own rationale).*

  only mechanically checks *across* `features/` folders, not within one).

  verbatim, no second, divergent failure-mapping implementation introduced.
- Re-checked that `ChatTitleDeriver`, the one domain helper RNF07 specifically needs to be independently
  testable, has zero constructor dependencies and zero I/O — confirmed pure in data-model.md's own listing.
- Re-checked the routing change (`app_router.dart`'s `/home` builder) against Principle V/research.md R7: no
  new `go_router` route, no `sessionId` path parameter — `AppRoutes.home` itself is unchanged.
- No change surfaces that touches `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, `.env`, any native iOS project file,

# Tasks: P-RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/007-chat-memory-rag/`
**Prerequisites**: plan.md, spec.md, research.md, data-model.md, contracts/, quickstart.md (all present)

**Tests**: Included. `plan.md`'s Constitution Check marks RNF07 (domain coverage ≥80%) and RNF09 (Either +
15/15 error scenarios) both "PASS (gate carried into tasks)", and every file under `contracts/` carries its own
"Test scenarios this contract owns" table plus `quickstart.md`'s "Automated checks" section — this is this
feature's own design material requesting test tasks, not an invented addition.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story (spec.md's five User Stories: P1, P1, P2, P2, P3). This
feature introduces one entirely new feature folder (`lib/features/chat/`, two blocs) plus two `core/network/`
extensions. Loading a conversation (resume-last / switch / new-empty) is needed by every single story — even
US4's "Novo Chat" and US5's offline browsing go through the same `_loadSession` path — so the shared
transport/data/repository layer and `ChatBloc`'s own "load a conversation" machinery are necessarily
Foundational; each User Story phase then adds that story's own handler bodies, widgets, and tests on top.

## Path Conventions

Single Flutter project (plan.md's "Project Type"): `lib/features/chat/{domain,data,presentation}/`, mirrored
under `test/features/chat/...`; two `core/network/` files extended in place; `lib/features/home/` extended in
place. No `backend/`/`frontend/` split, no `.env`/native project file touched, no change to
`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml` (Constraints, FR-014).

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - Getting an answer grounded in your own journal (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: send a message into a conversation (creating its session lazily on the first send, FR-010), stream a
RAG-grounded response, and have the full exchange persist across a restart — without ever creating a journal
entry (FR-001/FR-002/FR-003).

**Independent Test**: seed a prior entry on a specific topic, send a chat message that references that topic
without quoting it, and confirm the agent's response reflects that entry's content; confirm the exchange
survives leaving the screen and a full app restart; confirm "Meus Registros" gained no new entry from it.

## Phase 4: User Story 2 - Always knowing what the agent is doing (Priority: P1)

**Goal**: the three response states (streaming / complete / error) are always visually distinguishable, and a
response interrupted mid-stream never disappears (FR-004/FR-005/FR-007).

**Independent Test**: send a message and observe the UI progress through the streaming indicator into complete
or error; force a connection drop mid-response and confirm the partial text stays visible with a failure
indication instead of disappearing.

> The three-state rendering (`chat_message_bubble.dart`, T017) and the partial-content-preserving failure path
> (`_applyFailure` inside `_consumeTurn`, T022) are already built as shared Foundational/US1 infrastructure —
> `_consumeTurn` is one function handling both the success and failure branches of a turn, so it cannot be
> split across phases. This phase's own job is the scenario-specific tests that prove each contract, exactly
> as this story's own Acceptance Scenarios describe observing already-built behavior rather than new code.

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: no dependencies — can start immediately. **BLOCKS** every user story phase (every
  story needs `ChatBloc`'s "load a conversation" machinery at minimum).
- **User Story 1 (Phase 3)**: depends on Foundational only. MVP.
- **User Story 2 (Phase 4)**: depends on Foundational **and** US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022) — its failure-handling
  branch is built as part of that same function and cannot be split; this phase is otherwise test-only.
- **User Story 3 (Phase 5)**: depends on Foundational and US1's `_consumeTurn` (T022), which it reuses verbatim
  for the retry's own stream consumption.
- **User Story 4 (Phase 6)**: depends on Foundational only — independent of US1/US2/US3's own tasks (no shared
  code with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery).
- **User Story 5 (Phase 7)**: depends on Foundational's `_loadSession`/`ChatSessionsBloc` cache-fallback logic
  (already built there) and on `ChatComposer` (T023, US1) for its own offline-disabling test.
- **Polish (Phase 8)**: depends on all five user stories being complete.

### Within Each Phase

- Tasks touching the *same* file (`chat_bloc.dart`, `home_chat_shell_page.dart`, `app_drawer.dart`,
  `service_locator.dart`, `app_router.dart`) are listed in the sequential order they must be applied.
- Tasks creating a *new* file with no dependency on that phase's other new files are marked `[P]`.
- Test tasks are marked `[P]` relative to each other (distinct test files); each still depends on its
  corresponding implementation task(s) existing to pass.

### Parallel Opportunities

- T001, T004–T009, T014, T015, T017 (Foundational's entities/events/states/widgets/transport) can all run in
  parallel — ten independent files with no cross-dependencies among them.
- T011 and T012 (local cache, remote data source) can run in parallel with each other once T001–T009 land.
- All test tasks within a single user story phase can run in parallel with each other.
- User Story 4 (side menu) can be implemented in parallel with User Stories 1–3 (the live conversation) by a
  second developer, since neither `ChatSessionsBloc` nor `AppDrawer`'s "CONVERSAS" section shares any code path
  with `ChatBloc`'s turn-consumption machinery.

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (transport, data layer, entities, `ChatBloc`'s conversation-loading core).
2. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1 (lazy session creation, send, stream, persist, no entry created).
3. **STOP and VALIDATE**: seed a prior entry, send a related message, confirm the grounded response (SC-001);
   restart the app and confirm the exchange persists (SC-005).
4. Demo/ship if ready — this alone delivers RF04's "entire premise" (spec.md, User Story 1's "Why this
   priority").

### Incremental Delivery

1. Foundational → User Story 1 (MVP: grounded, persisted conversation).
2. + User Story 2 (the three-state visual contract — mostly tests over already-built engine behavior).
3. + User Story 3 (tap-to-retry on a failed response).
4. + User Story 4 (side menu: list, paginate, "Novo Chat") — independently buildable in parallel with 2–3.
5. + User Story 5 (offline banner + multi-conversation offline coverage).
6. + Polish (verification gates, manual walkthrough).

Each stage adds value without breaking the previous one, matching spec.md's own stated priority order (P1, P1,
P2, P2, P3).

## Test scenarios this contract owns

| # | Scenario | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ChatStarted` with no `lastActiveSessionId` stored | `ChatReady(sessionId: null, messages: [])` — no repository call beyond the one `lastActiveSessionId` read |
| 2 | `ChatStarted` with a stored id whose `listMessages` succeeds | `ChatReady(sessionId: ..., messages: [...])` |
| 3 | `ChatStarted` with a stored id whose `listMessages` fails and nothing is cached | `ChatReady(..., loadFailure: failure)` — the no-content edge case |
| 4 | `ChatStarted` with a stored id whose `listMessages` fails but a cache exists | `ChatReady(..., messages: <cached>)`, no `loadFailure` |
| 5 | `MessageSubmitted` on an empty conversation | optimistic user+assistant appended within the same synchronous `emit` (RNF01), *then* `createSession` is called with the derived title, *then* `sendMessage` |
| 6 | `MessageSubmitted` while offline | the composer was already disabled (`canSend == false`), so the handler is a no-op; confirms no repository call fires regardless |
| 7 | A full successful turn: `MessageCreated` → `TokenReceived` × N → `StreamDone` | the assistant message's `content` grows incrementally per token, then is replaced by `StreamDone.content` exactly, `status: complete`, `awaitingResponse: false` |
| 8 | A turn interrupted by `Left(NetworkOfflineFailure)` after 2 tokens | the assistant message keeps its 2-tokens-worth of partial content, `status: failed`, `awaitingResponse: false` (FR-005) |
| 9 | `MessageRetryRequested` on a `failed` message not at the end of the conversation (Edge Cases) | only that one message's position is replaced; every later message in `messages` is untouched |
| 10 | Two `MessageRetryRequested` dispatched back-to-back for the same message (simulating a double-tap before the composer visually disables) | the second dispatch is a no-op (`current.awaitingResponse` is already `true` from the first) |
| 11 | `NewConversationRequested` while a previous conversation has unsaved-to-disk messages in memory | the previous conversation's own cache entry (`ChatLocalCache`) is untouched — only `lastActiveSessionId` changes; reselecting it later still shows its full history |
| 12 | A `_ConnectivityChanged(false)` event arrives mid-turn (device goes offline while a response is streaming) | `isOffline` becomes `true` immediately; the in-flight turn is **not** aborted by this alone — it still resolves via whatever `sendMessage`'s own stream eventually yields (a real disconnect surfaces as its own `NetworkOfflineFailure` item from `ApiClient.sseStream`, not from this separate connectivity event) |
| 13 | `ConversationSelected`/`NewConversationRequested` dispatched while a turn is mid-stream for the conversation being left | the in-flight turn's later `TokenReceived`/`StreamDone`/`Left` items are ignored (generation mismatch) — the newly-loaded conversation's state is never mutated by the abandoned turn |
